name: Required Reason: UserDefaults
plain: iOS UserDefaults access needs a reason code such as CA92.1 (app only) or 1C8F.1 (app group).
meaning: Shared defaults can leak info across apps. CA92.1 is app-only data, 1C8F.1 is data shared in one app group, C56D.1 is an SDK wrapper, AC6B.1 reads managed configuration.

android.api_surface: Android has no gate: SharedPreferences is app-private

ios.revocation: App Review: reason must match use
ios.api_surface: CA92.1 app-only; 1C8F.1 same app group; C56D.1 SDK wrapper only; AC6B.1 managed app config

limits.headline: Can keep its own saved settings on iPhone, but must give Apple a reason
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app stores settings quietly as you use it
can: Save its own settings and choices, with a stated reason on iPhone
Share settings with apps in the same developer group on iPhone
Save settings on Android with no gate, in the app's own private area
cannot: Use it to see other apps' settings; the data stays in the app or its group
Skip the stated reason on iPhone; App Store review checks it
Use it to track you across other developers' apps
Share settings across developers on Android
limits.differs: Android keeps preferences app private and has no gate. iPhone needs a declared reason code.

story.what_it_is: iOS makes apps give an approved reason before using a shared settings store.

marketing.name: Required Reason APIs
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps must declare why they use UserDefaults, since shared defaults can leak information across apps.

story.for_you: You never see it. UserDefaults is where apps save small settings. Apple makes apps explain why they use it, so no app quietly reads another app's data.
story.for_makers: Makers choose a reason code, like CA92.1 for the app's own data or 1C8F.1 for an app group. Sharing across companies is not allowed.

use_cases.example: A notes app saves your theme choice and declares CA92.1.
A game saves your sound setting and declares CA92.1.
A work app reads settings set by a company manager and declares AC6B.1.
An SDK wraps defaults for the app and declares C56D.1.
A music app shares settings with its widget through an app group and declares 1C8F.1.
A tracker that reads settings shared with other apps is flagged.

story.ios_note: Enforced through the privacy manifest and App Store checks.

technical_bounds: Cannot read data of other apps
